summary: Variant analysis of R1-O2-1/R1-O2-2. I listed every durable artifact of the stored player, the bridge and crisium. For each I worked out when it is synced, what a kill or a power loss at each step leaves, and what a relaunch trusts. Outside the two confirmed sites (revert_interrupted_input branch 1, and the removal of machine.revert on a sealed reopen) I found no other place that reloads a directory O2 does not guarantee or deletes the only guaranteed copy. Each artifact is checked below. Only two Low candidates remain, both about records outside the machines.
artifact_inventory: machine/ (epoch machine): loaded with SHARING_ALL between commits, so between inputs O2 does not guarantee it; machine.revert is then the guaranteed copy. commit_epoch_state and seal_epoch_state run destroy and then sync_stored before writing state.json. Relaunch: branch 2 loads it only when the backup does not rehash to root, and every such window falls after a destroy and a sync. Branch 1 is R1-O2-1/R1-O2-2.

machine.revert: stored_machine_pair:commit clones it under its final name and syncs only afterwards (R1-O2-1). It is removed on a sealed reopen (R1-O2-2). The rejection revert (stored_machine_pair:revert) clones from it without a sync but never deletes it, and commit_epoch_state syncs machine/ before the next state.json.

entries/K: clone_loaded_directory destroys the machine, clones, runs sync_stored on the clone (which syncs its files, the directory and entries/), and never loads the entry with sharing. Relaunch trusts only entries named by the machine-cache-K.json that state.json names; other entries are removed. Units load clones in pair/ without clear_hash_tree, which is acceptable because the entries are guaranteed.
pair/, pair.revert, agreed/, agreed.revert: process-local working copies; reopen force-removes them (pair always, agreed in the sealed path, and an open epoch has no agreed pair).

checkpoints/epoch-N+1: written by machine:store into <dir>.tmp, then sync_stored, durable manifest files and a directory sync, then rename_stored (which syncs the parent). An existing checkpoint is reused without a check, and only a reorg past the input policy or an earlier R1-O2-1 corruption could make it stale. The player clones it and loads it with clear_hash_tree.

checkpoint removal (remove_epoch_files): rename to .removed first, completed at startup. Removal happens only after an epoch is finished (its settlement is irreversible) and keep_epochs older; no later epoch reads an older checkpoint.

state.json: write_durable_file (tmp, fsync, rename) followed by a directory sync, and it is the single commit point. Every file it names (frontier-K, outputs-frontier-K, machine-cache-K, last-output-C, mcycle-forest, uarch-i-p) is written durably and its directory synced before state.json. Only afterwards are files the previous state.json named and evicted entries removed.

forests/*: content-addressed tree files written with write_durable_file. Children are made durable before a parent replaces an existing file, and the frontier file is the commit point. Reopen removes only .tmp. files from forests in use, and expansions only add files.
inputs/N.bin: clone_file, sync_file and a directory sync on receipt. Reopen removes inputs at or past input_count, and the listener delivers them again.
journal.json (prt-transactions): written durably, and its directory synced, before every publication. Reload checks its consistency. See candidate 1.
state/ and state/epoch-N directories: created with fs.create_directory, and nothing syncs their entries in the parent. See candidate 2.
status file and pid file: never read back by the player.

candidates.title: After a relaunch, a journal candidate that was signed and stored but never broadcast (stop between journal store and eth_sendRawTransaction) still throttles that job's first real publication for up to bump_blocks blocks
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); stands in for the honest operator's transaction submission.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:submit, lines 184-191 (same-job throttle on record.last_attempt) and 284-288 (store() before publish()); M.new lines 326-359 (the reloaded journal keeps last_attempt).
candidates.description: submit records last_attempt = {block = tip} and the candidate, stores the journal durably, and only then publishes. If the process stops in between, the reloaded journal claims a publication at block B that never reached any node. On the first tick after the relaunch, submit finds previous.job == intent.key and a canonical last_attempt with tip - B < bump_blocks, so it returns {waiting = true}. A response the node never received is held back until bump_blocks blocks after B. The code already asks the node whether it holds a candidate (eth_getTransactionByHash), but only at the fee ceiling (lines 193-208), not before applying the bump throttle. The relaunch therefore trusts a durable record whose content does not match what happened, which is a variant of trusting state O2 does not guarantee.
candidates.trigger: A host stop (kill or power loss) of the honest validator between self:store() and chain:publish() for a deadline-bound job, then a relaunch by prt-supervise.sh. No adversary action is needed.
candidates.reachability: Reached on the honest operator's path ('Restarting after a stop (O2)') at any submission. The extra delay is at most bump_blocks (default 3) blocks after the stored attempt, minus the blocks the relaunch itself takes (process start and a rehash of each reopened epoch's backup). The same throttle after a failed publication is intended and tested (prt-transactions-test.lua lines 158-179); the restart case is not.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: not excluded. A process stop is the ordinary O2 case, and the journal is the player's own record, not a stored machine directory. 2. Role: Support. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. 3. High/Medium cases: Medium applies only if the stood-in rating is High or Critical. The delay is a bounded constant number of blocks per stop, far below Dave's clock allowances, so it removes no margin the goal relies on. 4. Critical in the stood-in role: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks. After a stop, it restarts ... and keeps defending its claim'. It is violated only if a stop falls within bump_blocks of a deadline, and the stop and the restart time would already cost comparable time. I do not claim a violation. 5. Low: a real defect (a relaunch trusts a journal entry about a broadcast that never happened) that breaks no rule in practice.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Negligible. At most a few extra blocks before an honest response after a crash, which could matter only for a stop right next to a deadline.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. prt-transactions-test.lua shows the throttle is intended after a publication error (it mines bump_blocks blocks before the retry), and no test covers a reload of a never-broadcast candidate.
candidates.test_idea: Mock chain object (rpc, head, is_canonical, simulate, publish) as in prt-transactions-test.lua. Make publish raise on the first call, after store(), to model the stop. Create a new manager from the same journal path and call submit with the same intent at tip+1, with eth_getTransactionByHash returning null. Assert that it publishes (returns published=true) instead of {waiting=true}.

candidates.title: crisium creates the state directory and each epoch directory without syncing their parent, so on filesystems that do not order metadata a power loss can drop a directory (and a first run's journal) whose contents were all fsynced
candidates.component: PRT player process, doc/recipes/crisium.lua (with prt.lua create_epoch_directory)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: PRT player and bridge); stands in for the honest operator's storing and restart.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua lines 137-139 (fs.create_directory(options.state)) and 176-178 (fs.create_directory(epoch_directory)); prt.lua create_epoch_directory (lines 2839-2845) syncs the epoch directory itself, never state/. prt-transactions methods:store syncs state/ but not its parent.
candidates.description: Each durable file in the epoch directory is fsynced and its directory synced, and sync_stored syncs '<machine>/..', which is the epoch directory. The entry of state/epoch-N in state/, and of state/ in its parent, is never fsynced. POSIX requires an fsync of the parent to make a new entry durable. Without it, a power loss can lose a whole epoch directory even after state.json committed inside it. On a first run it can also lose state/ itself, journal.json included, although that journal was written durably before a transaction was broadcast. Consequences on relaunch: (a) the epoch is recomputed from its checkpoint, which is correct but costs a full epoch replay while its dispute runs. (b) Without the journal, M.new starts with no accounts, and submit's first-account check 'exclusive signer already has untracked pending transactions' fails for as long as the broadcast transaction stays pending, so the validator crash-loops and cannot answer until that transaction is mined or dropped.
candidates.trigger: A power loss shortly after crisium creates state/ (first run) or state/epoch-N (when a new epoch's listener opens), on a filesystem that does not make a new directory entry durable through an fsync of a file inside it.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable on ext4 or XFS in practice, because an fsync of a child forces the journal or log, which already holds the earlier mkdir. Btrfs logs new parent directories on fsync. So this is a POSIX-level gap with very low practical reachability. No adversary is involved.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: possibly 'Host faults ... as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash'. No wrong hash results; the effects are recomputation or a temporary refusal to start. O2 names power loss as an ordinary stop. 2. Role: Support (AUDIT.md table). 3. High/Medium: Medium only if it would rate High or Critical in the honest role; the practical effect is bounded and the filesystems the manual targets (reflink: XFS, btrfs) are not affected in practice. 4. Critical in the stood-in role would need R4 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim' to fail. It fails only in the journal case while a transaction is pending on a non-ordering filesystem. 5. Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Negligible on the filesystems the manual expects. On a filesystem with unordered metadata, a relaunch could lose an epoch's progress (recomputed) or, on a first run, its nonce journal, which blocks restart while a transaction is pending.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (crisium.lua, prt.lua create_epoch_directory and sync paths, src/machine.cpp sync_stored syncing dir and dir/.., prt-transactions store).
candidates.test_idea: Use an strace-based syscall check like R1-O2-2's check (A): run a crisium-like setup that creates state/ and state/epoch-0, commits state.json and a journal, and assert that the parent of each newly created directory was fsynced after the mkdir and before the first publication.

not_covered: Real power-loss injection (dm-log-writes or similar) on XFS/btrfs with reflinks. All crash reasoning here is code reading against O2's definition; I ran no experiment.
I did not run the player-restart runner. I read the logs of the earlier fixed and random runs (both settled) and did not re-run them to avoid the shared chain.

The phtc 'initialized' tag protocol and whether a destroyed SHARING_ALL machine always leaves dht/dpt/sht/phtc consistent before sync. I relied on earlier O2 hunters' conclusions; the guarantees of entries and checkpoints rest on it.

The cartesi-machine CLI --revert-mode=stored (read only: tmp+sync+rename, consistent with the manual) and run-rolling-calculator-from-storage.lua (consistent). I did not test their combinations with --store or clone: options.
Reuse of an existing checkpoint without a check in store_next_epoch_checkpoint. It matters only after a reorg past the input policy or an earlier corrupted restart, so I did not pursue it.
Dishonest players (prt-dishonest.lua) sharing the demo's checkpoints directory with the honest player's removals (out of scope).
Windows/macOS persistence paths; fsync error semantics; EMLINK and hard-link fallback of read-only files across many clones.
The forest store's merge path with lazily loaded children (550fd3c), checked by reading only; no randomized crash test of frontier_forest_store or expansions.
The bridge's in-memory state after a restart (prepared, invalid and rejected tables) and its interaction with the journal beyond candidate 1.
Restart cost (a full rehash with clear_hash_tree of every reopened epoch's backup, plus a clone and sync on each relaunch) against R12's per-restart bound: judged bounded, not measured.
